title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The diff does not contain any SQL query construction or database query operations. It only adds test cases and permission checks using Django's ORM and permission framework, which use parameterized queries internally.

The diff adds proper authorization checks to multiple stream management endpoints. Each endpoint (GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE, POST for verify and status operations) now validates that the requesting user has the 'authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream' permission on the SSFProvider object before proceeding. These checks are placed before object retrieval, preventing unauthorized access. The test file validates that users without this permission receive 403 Forbidden responses.

evidence.content:
def test_stream_get(self):
        """get stream without add_stream permission"""
        self.assertFalse(self.user.has_perm("authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream", self.provider))
        stream = Stream.objects.create(provider=self.provider)
        res = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "authentik_providers_ssf:stream",
                kwargs={"application_slug": self.application.slug},
            ),
            HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f"Bearer {self.token.token}",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 403)
